```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
# Bash chunks are a record of commands you ran in the Terminal. Knitting shows
# them but doesn't run them again.
knitr::opts_hooks$set(engine = function(options) {
  if (options$engine == "bash") options$eval <- FALSE
  options
})
```

Notes for [Workshop 1](https://mb5370.bioinformatics.guide/workshop1.html). Run the commands for this workshop in the Terminal, from inside the `command_line` folder:

```{bash}
cd ~/mb5370-workshops/command_line
pwd
```

Replace the text below each heading with your own notes. Copy each command you run into a bash chunk like the one above.

## Basic unix commands

Notes on `pwd`, `ls`, `cd` and how unix commands are put together.
```{bash}
ls #lists all the files in the working directory
ls -1 #lists all the files with 1 entry per line
ls -1r #lists in reverse
cd #to change the working directory by inputting the desired file path 
pwd #always use with 'cd' to check what your working directory is
```
## Viewing and searching files

Notes on `cat`, `head`, `grep` and `man`.
```{bash}
cd ~/mb5370-workshops/command_line
echo $'>fasta_header\nMMGTSRCVILLFALLLWAANAAPPEIHTTRPNVPEEIKRPNSTEIETPAVKQLETPSIFL\nLTTLEVAEADVDSTLETMKDRNKKNSAKLSKIGNNMKSLLSVFSVFGGFLSLLSVVTTTS' > test.fasta

cat test.fasta #to view the file
head -2 test.fasta #to view only the first two lines #default is first 10 lines

grep '^>' test.fasta #globally search a regular expression and print; finds lines matching specific strings in files; this specific one is to find the fasta header

grep KDRNKKNSAK test.fasta #to look up a sepcific amino acid sequence 

man grep #to view the manual and look up useful flags
grep -n KDRNKKNSAK test.fasta #to report line number of matches
grep -i kdrnkknsak test.fasta #case insensitive match
grep -c KDRNKKNSAK test.fasta #count all files that contain that pattern
grep -w KDRNKKNSAK test.fasta #match whole words only
```
## Sequence file formats

Notes on the fasta and fastq formats. 
fasta<- Consists of 1 or more entries each of which consists of a header and a sequence. Each entry has a title line and a sequence. Multiple entries can be stored in a  single file. Line 1 starts with > and holds the sequence ID. Line 2 (or several lines, for long sequences) holds the sequence itself.
fastq<- Designed for storing sequencing data along with quality scores. Like fasta but with additional information about the reliabilty of each base. Mostly used to store outputs from sequencing instruments. Each entry has 4 lines. Often millions of entries. 1. @ followed by the read I 2. The sequence 3.+ (optionally repeating the ID) 4. Quality string, with one character per base
